result: Photoaffinity labelling and native gel-permeation HPLC of CFS PBMC found subsets with 2-5A-dependent RNase L activity only at 37/30 kDa versus 80 and 42 kDa in controls.
reason: Same lab as cited Suhadolnik 1994 (not independent); adds detail on the low-MW RNase L species and patient subsets

result: In 23 CFS patients vs controls on an autonomic test battery, CFS showed significant baseline increases (abstract truncated) and altered sympathetic and parasympathetic measures, possibly from deconditioning or postviral autonomic neuropathy.
reason: Small early autonomic case-control study consistent with altered resting HR/vagal measures; abstract truncated

result: At 10-year follow-up of a 1984 West Otago outbreak, 10 of 21 (48%) met CDC CFS criteria and most (16) had returned to premorbid activity, suggesting better prognosis for epidemic-associated CFS.
reason: Long-term outcome data for an epidemic-onset subgroup with apparently better recovery; small, mixed cohort

result: Systematic review of 26 studies: under 10% of adults with operationally defined CFS (5 studies) returned to premorbid function, while 54-94% of children recovered; poor prognosis linked to older age, chronicity, psychiatric comorbidity and physical attribution.
reason: Earlier systematic review (Joyce/Hotopf/Wessely) reaching the same low adult recovery estimate; overlaps studies with Cairns & Hotopf 2005

result: Among 153 fatigued referral patients, mean CRP, beta2-microglobulin and neopterin were higher in CFS than controls, with intercorrelated markers suggesting an immune-activated subset; sIL-2R and IL-6 not reported as different.
reason: Measures circulating CRP, which the meta-analysis finds elevated; supports subgroup interpretation

result: Polysomnography in 49 CFS vs 20 controls showed sleep-initiation and maintenance disturbance (longer sleep-onset latency, more stage shifts) and lower stage 4, independent of fibromyalgia or psychiatric comorbidity; REM latency normal.
reason: Same PSG measures (SOL, maintenance) in same direction; lower stage 4 differs from meta-analysis's higher N3

result: 20 CFS patients scored lower than 20 controls on reaction-time and processing-speed-dependent working-memory tests, similar to 14 depressed patients; day-1 testing did not reduce day-2 performance.
reason: Same processing-speed and working-memory deficits; note no next-day decline after cognitive effort

result: CDC case-control study of rigorously defined CFS found no difference in NK cell function, WBC counts, immunoglobulins, complement or mitogen proliferation; only marginal cytokine and surface-marker differences, larger in onset or symptom-state subgroups.
reason: Tests NK function and finds no difference

result: In 43 CFS trial participants, T-cell subsets, activation and naive/memory proportions did not differ from controls, NK cell (CD16+/CD56+/CD3-) and CD11b+ CD8 percentages were higher, and no immune measure changed with or predicted treatment response.
reason: Measures NK cell numbers (increased), not cytotoxicity; no atlas finding covers lymphocyte subset counts
